query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A single, targeted thermo‐mechanical processing step—specifically, a hybrid processing (e.g., initial cryo‐rolling followed by a controlled low‐temperature warm rolling)—will refine the naturally cast dual-phase lamellar colonies into a stable ultrafine dual-structure with coherent nano‐precipitates at the phase boundaries, simultaneously increasing dislocation storage (and thus back‐stress hardening) and inhibiting microcrack initiation, thereby improving both room-temperature yield strength and tensile ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) with a coarse lamellar colony structure comprising ductile (L12) and brittle (B2) phases that are prone to microcrack initiation along the internal boundaries.
generation.intervention: Apply a hybrid thermo-mechanical processing (such as cryo-rolling followed by annealing/warm rolling at a moderate temperature, e.g., around 600 °C) to induce a refined, ultrafine lamellar microstructure with coherent, nano-scale precipitates along the phase boundaries.
generation.conditions: The intervention is conducted on cast eutectic HEAs (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1) where the processing parameters (strain per pass, total strain ≈90% reduction equivalent, cryogenic rolling followed by controlled warmth) are optimized to retain the lamellar morphology while refining the interlamellar spacing and promoting coherent ordering without triggering unwanted recrystallization.
generation.structural_mediator: An ultrafine dual-phase lamellar structure with reduced (nanometric) interlamellar spacing and strengthened, chemically-disordered coherent interfaces (nano-precipitates) at the phase boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The refined lamellae lead to enhanced dislocation storage and an increased back-stress during deformation, while the coherent nano-precipitates at the phase boundaries suppress early microcrack initiation by reinforcing the interfaces. Together, these features delay localized plastic instability, thereby enhancing yield strength and ductility simultaneously.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the coarse as-cast lamellar baseline, the treated HEA will exhibit a statistically significant increase in both yield strength and room-temperature tensile ductility. In tensile tests, the processed alloy will show higher strain hardening rates and delayed crack propagation.
generation.baseline: The unmodified as-cast eutectic HEA, which features coarse lamellar colonies with poorly strengthened phase boundaries that lead to early microcracking and a pronounced strength–ductility trade-off.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected provided that the processing successfully refines the lamellar spacing without completely destroying the colony structure; excessive heat or strain that blurs the lamellar morphology or leads to over-recrystallization may negate the effect. The intervention is most applicable to alloys with similar eutectic lamellar arrangements (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi2.1).
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative enhancement of strength and ductility depends on the exact processing parameters (e.g., degree of deformation, annealing time/temperature), and the optimal conditions may require further experimental tuning. The extent to which coherent nano-precipitates contribute needs to be verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 samples: one set is the as-cast control and the other set is processed using the proposed hybrid thermo-mechanical route (cryo-rolling followed by warm rolling at ~600 °C, with total strain corresponding to ~90% reduction). Perform room-temperature tensile tests on both sets while characterizing the microstructure (using SEM/TEM) for interlamellar spacing and presence of coherent nano-precipitates along phase boundaries.
measurements: Microstructural metrics (lamellar spacing, interface coherence, precipitate size and distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in both yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast control, or if microstructural analysis does not reveal the formation of a refined, ultrafine lamellar structure with coherent nano-precipitates at the boundaries, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Realizing improved strength–ductility synergy in eutectic alloys acting as in situ composite materials remains a challenge in conventional eutectic systems, which is why eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), a newly-emerging multi-principal-element eutectic category, may offer wider in situ composite possibilities. Here, we use an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA to engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that deliberately inherits its composite lamellar nature by tailored thermo-mechanical processing to achieve property combinations which are not accessible to previously-reported reinforcement methodologies. The as-prepared samples exhibit hierarchically-structural heterogeneity due to phase decomposition, and the improved mechanical response during deformation is attributed to both a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism. This work provides a pathway for strengthening eutectic alloys and widens the design toolbox for high-performance materials based upon EHEAs. The present study focuses on the marginally hypo-eutectic HEA with the nominal composition of Al0.7CoCrFeNi (15 at. % Al and 21.25 at.% each of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni). While a few previous investigations on this HEA have reported a lamellar two-phase fcc/B2microstructure in this alloy, a detailed investigation of the microstructure of this alloy and its evolution during post-solidification thermo-mechanical processing forms the basis of the present study. Furthermore, the present study also investigates the influence of such heat-treatments on the mechanical behavior of this alloy under both quasi-static low strain rate tensile loading conditions, as well as dynamic strain rate compression conditions.
